chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Aquli, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
When the Qaim arises, people will deny him; he will return to them as a young man, and none will remain with him except every believer in whom Allah took the covenant in the first age of creation.

key_terms.الذَّرِّ الْأَوَّلِ: The first age of creation (primordial dust)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Twelfth Imam

ai.seo_question: Who will believe in Imam Al-Qaim when he reappears?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the paradox of the Mahdi’s reappearance: though he returns as a youthful figure, the masses will reject him due to spiritual blindness, while true believers are those who recognized the divine covenant (Mithaq) in the primordial realm of dust. This underscores the Shia concept that faith is not merely intellectual assent but a pre-eternal spiritual recognition, linking the Imam’s youth to vitality and the people’s denial to their failure to uphold the primordial pledge.
